newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soars to record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soars to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed 170.08 points, or 1.04 percent, to a record close of 16,541.60 on Wednesday on renewed interest in property stocks and record-breaking turnover, brokers said.
Market activity was centred chiefly on blue chip property stocks and China plays, both H shares and red chips, brokers said.
"The Cheung Kong group has reintroduced speculative appeal into the market and the restructuring theme," said a broker with a U.S. house.

Cheung Kong and Hutchison, which together acquired three percent stakes in Singapore-listed Jardine Matheson and Hongkong Land, also sparked investors' interest in getting the real asset value out of the market's property stocks, the U.S. broker said.
The property sector led the market, followed by the commercial and industrial sector.

Cheung Kong leaped to a new high of HK$92.25 then eased to close HK$4.50 higher at HK$92.00. Hutchison Whampoa also jumped to a new high of HK$82.75, before falling back to close HK$2.50 higher at HK$81.25.
Institututional favourite Sun Hung Kai Properties climbed to a record of HK$109.50, then eased to close just HK$0.50 higher at HK$106.00.
"Investors are rerating these stocks, revising net asset values upwards," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel.
H share Yizheng Chemical rose HK$0.55 to close at HK$3.125 on the possibility of a group restructuring, analysts said.
Most brokers were optimistic the market's results period rally would continue.
"I think with this turnover, the rally will continue," said McAllister. "The market has the momentum to go higher."

But others were cautious. "I am still bullish, but after this sharp increase, I would like to see a correction before recommending anyone buy this market," said Peter Lui in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
